Conversely choosing preimages in one such source block per occupied target defines g on the image and allows a partition-preserving extension everywhere. With the union fixed at size s, subtract the product of the numbers of non-surjections into it from all tuples of block maps into it. An onto component guarantees that this chosen set really is the union; distinct targets are independent. The multinomial allocation of m labelled source blocks to m labelled targets gives m![z^m] A_n(z)^m and exponentiating the resulting coefficients gives (3). For fixed n>=2 the normalized local weights p_k=c_n(k)/n^(nk) are positive, p_0=p_1=1, and p_2<1 (two distinct constant images). The mean of the tilted lattice law is strictly increasing because its derivative with respect to log t is the variance; its limits are zero and infinity, the latter by the unique leading e^t term. At the tilt of mean one the law has span one and positive finite variance, so the lattice local CLT and Stirling cancel the sqrt(2 pi m) factor and yield precisely 1/sqrt(v_n) times rho_n^m. The minimizing ratio B_n(t)/t is no greater than B_n(1)<e, ensuring rho_n<1. For n=1 all maps are regular, as in the full transformation monoid.
